methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Sensory Storytelling
content: Problem: Students often write "flat" stories describing only actions (I went, I played).

Solution: This week introduces the "Perception" group of irregular verbs (saw, heard, felt, smelt). By integrating the 5 senses into storytelling, students learn to add descriptive depth to their past tense narratives.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce the 4 perception verbs using a forest adventure context. Focus on meaning and spelling.
Session 2: Practice using the verbs with descriptive adjectives (loud sound, soft leaves).
Session 3: Full production. Write a cohesive sensory recount of a past trip incorporating sequence words.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show a flashcard (e.g., ear). Student must provide the past tense verb ("heard") and a logical sentence ("I heard a dog.").

Communicative task (Step 5 - 10 min): The Sense Detective. Student A lists three sensory clues ("I saw trees. I heard birds. I smelt flowers."). Student B must guess the location ("You went to the forest!").

listening_script.speed_note: Read aloud at a normal, clear pace (85 wpm). Pause 2–3 seconds between sentences. Read the full text twice before students answer questions.
listening_script.text: Last Sunday, Leo walked in the forest. First, he saw a tall tree with green leaves. Then, he heard a loud monkey. Next, he felt the cool wind on his face. Finally, he smelt the rain coming. He ran home quickly!

teacher_contents.speaking_notes:
SPEAKING CHECKPOINT — Teacher Guidance (do NOT share with students):

Student A: Names one thing Max saw in the forest (e.g., "Max saw tall trees and colorful birds").
Student B: Names one thing Max heard (e.g., "He heard the birds singing").
Goal: Use saw and heard correctly — two distinct perception verbs in past tense.

PULL-OUT TASK (S1):
— Show a forest picture. Ask: "If you were Max, what would you SEE? What would you HEAR?"
— Scaffold weaker students: "I SAW ___. I HEARD ___."
— Target elicitation: saw / heard — confirm students DON'T say "seed" or "heared".

COMMUNICATIVE TASK TIP:
— Model immediately if errors occur: "We say SAW (not 'seed') and HEARD (not 'heared')."
— Stronger students: chain all four verbs: "I saw ___, heard ___, felt ___, smelt ___."
teacher_contents.stem_extension:
STEM/CLIL Extension Notes (teacher only):

PART 6: STEM/CLIL CONNECTION — The 5 Senses
Our Five Senses
Read this: We use our five senses to learn about the world. We SEE with our eyes. We HEAR with our ears. We SMELL with our nose. We TASTE with our tongue. We FEEL with our skin. When you walk in a forest, you can use all your senses. You can see trees, hear birds, and smell flowers!
Inquiry task: What part of your body do you use to hear the birds? ________________________________________
teacher_contents.in_class_speaking:
IN-CLASS SPEAKING ACTIVITIES — Session 1 (teacher-led)

Activity 1 — Pair Speaking (3–5 min, pairs):
  Student A: Name a sense verb ("I heard...").
  Student B: Finish the sentence logically ("...a loud dog!").

Challenge Extension (L3 — for advanced/older students):
  [O] L3 — Fill in the blank with 3 options (8 items)
  Last week, I _______________ (see / saw / seen) a rabbit.
  I _______________ (hear / heard / hearing) a funny sound.
  She _______________ (feel / felt / feeling) the cold water.
  We _______________ (smell / smelt / smelling) the good food.
  They walked in the dark _______________ (forest / ocean / sky).
  The bird flew and I _______________ (saw / felt / smelt) it.
  I touched the blanket and it _______________ (heard / felt / saw) soft.
  The music was loud, so we _______________ (smelt / heard / saw) it clearly.
  [O] L4 — Sentence Expansion (8 items)
  Base: I saw. + Add: (a colorful bird) → ________________________________________
  Base: I heard. + Add: (the wind blowing) → ________________________________________
teacher_contents.vc_answer_key: [1] everyone [2] name [3] ten [4] forest [5] family [6] senses [7] saw [8] sky [9] heard [10] wind [11] felt [12] smelt [13] amazing
teacher_contents.reading_passage: Last weekend, Max went to the forest with his father. "I saw tall trees! I saw colorful birds! I saw a small rabbit!" said Max. He heard the birds singing. He heard the wind in the trees. It sounded magical. Max felt very happy in the forest. He smelt the fresh pine trees. "The forest smells amazing!" he said. It was the best day.
teacher_contents.grammar_notes:
• see→saw, hear→heard, feel→felt, smell→smelt — four perception/sense verbs
• All four are irregular; 'smelt' is the British English irregular form (smelled is also accepted)
• Error prevention: 'seed' ✗ → saw ✓ | 'heared' ✗ → heard ✓ | 'feeled' ✗ → felt ✓
• Teaching tip: link each verb to a sense — saw (eyes), heard (ears), felt (hands/skin), smelt (nose)
• Contrast: 'saw' = past of SEE (not 'seen' — that is past participle, not Past Simple)

Goal: Question-and-answer using heard / saw — accuracy under mild pressure.

DIFFERENTIATION:

— Stronger students: tell the whole story using: heard / saw / felt / smelt (if applicable).

teacher_contents.reading_passage: Yesterday evening, Luna went for a walk near the forest. First, she heard a very loud sound. It was an owl! Then, she saw a small shadow moving in the grass. It was a cute rabbit. Luna walked closer to the river. She felt the cool water on her hands. It felt refreshing. Suddenly, she smelt something sweet in the air — it was wild flowers! teacher_contents.grammar_notes:
• Session 2 reinforcement: heard / saw / felt / smelt all appear in Luna's evening walk
• Two uses of 'felt': felt the water (physical sensation) + felt peaceful (emotion) — both correct
• Pair contrast: Luna HEARD a sound (past) vs. she HEARS sounds every day (present)
• Spiral review: Luna WENT for a walk (W29 go→went) + W31 sense verbs — two-week link
• Grammar chain for class: 'Luna went, heard, saw, felt, and smelt.' — 5 irregular verbs in one sentence

SPEAKING CHECKPOINT — Teacher Guidance:

Student A: Names something Max saw on the mountain hike (e.g., "He saw a waterfall").
Student B: Names something Max heard (e.g., "He heard a loud roar").
Goal: Full W31 mastery — saw / heard / felt across a connected adventure story.

PULL-OUT TASK (S3 — Communicative Task):

— Mastery check: all three verbs used correctly with sequence words.

DIFFERENTIATION:
— Weaker students: provide verb prompts — point to SAW / HEARD / FELT cards.
— Stronger students: add smelt — "What did the mountain smell like? Max SMELT fresh pine trees."

teacher_contents.reading_passage: Last Sunday, Max and his dad went on a hike up the mountain. First, Max saw a beautiful waterfall. The water was very clear and bright. Then, they walked higher. Suddenly, Max heard a loud roar. He was scared! "Don't worry," dad said. "It's just the wind." Next, Max felt the cold mountain air. He smelt fresh pine trees. Finally, he felt very brave and proud.
teacher_contents.grammar_notes:
• Full W31 mastery: saw / heard / felt / smelt all in one mountain adventure story
• 'felt' used twice again: felt the cold air (sensation) + felt brave (emotion) — reinforces dual use
• Error focus this session: 'he seed the waterfall' is a very common student error → always 'SAW'
• Spiral: W29 (went) + W30 (ate, drank, had) + W31 (saw, heard, felt, smelt) = 8 irregular verbs total
• Communicative task: students retell the hike using all 4 sense verbs — mastery checkpoint
